member.name: T:SimulaSharp.Kernel.Attributes.TriggerableAttribute
member.summary:
Marks a void method on an interface used as a [CrossReference<T>] target as fire-and-forget. On the generated <T>Ref the method returns void: a same-site caller invokes the target directly (inline, immediately), while a cross-site caller Posts the call onto the target's dispatcher and returns at once — there is no result to await. Use it for one-way notifications / commands (the "notify" tier), where the async request/response surface (the default) would be needless overhead.

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.Kernel.Attributes.VolatileAccessAttribute
member.summary:
Marks a get-only property on an interface used as a [CrossReference<T>] target as a live gauge. On the generated <T>Ref the property is a plain synchronous getter that reads the target directly — no dispatch, no Task, no marshalling, no cache — so a caller on any thread reads the freshest value with a single lock-free memory read (the "gauge" tier). Use it for a continuously-changing scalar (e.g. a live power draw) that would be wasteful to pull through the async request/response surface.
The property must be get-only and of an atomically-readable type (a word-size primitive, an enum, or a reference) — a larger struct can tear under a cross-thread read. Its freshness guarantee is producer-side: the implementing model must back the getter with a volatile read of a single-producer field. A gauge read is not ordered against [Triggerable] notifications — it bypasses the dispatcher entirely. This attribute is a pure code-generation hint on the interface contract; it is invisible to tooling that reads the model's structure.

member.name: M:SimulaSharp.Kernel.Services.SimulatorBase.Dispose
member.summary: Tears the simulation down (single-use, no reset). Order matters for the park-on-idle sites: the clock thread wakes a site by Set()ting its wait handle (per-tick horizon wakes and the stop handler), so it must be fully stopped before those handles are disposed. So: pause the clock (park its thread, and fire the stop handlers under control), stop every site thread, run each service's then each model's deinit while nothing is executing, dispose (join) the clock, then — only now that no thread can touch them — dispose the site wait handles.
